note_tweet.text:
Pennsylvania just reported its sixth measles death.
The woman was not vaccinated.
Health officials in Pennsylvania confirmed the death of an unvaccinated 39-year-old woman, marking the sixth measles-related fatality in the state during the current outbreak.
The resident of Franklin County had underlying health conditions and suffered a fatal cardiac event linked to complications from a recent measles diagnosis.
Pennsylvania has now logged over 1,100 cases and more than 200 hospitalizations since the outbreak began, making it the focal point of the nation's largest measles surge in decades.
Public health experts stress that the escalating cases and fatalities demonstrate the serious risks associated with falling immunization rates.
Although measles was declared eliminated in the United States in 2000 due to high vaccination coverage, declining MMR vaccination levels in key regions have enabled the virus to resurface. Medical professionals continue to emphasize that full immunization remains the single most effective barrier against severe complications and community spread.
source: Luscombe, R. (2026). Pennsylvania announces sixth death in measles outbreak as case numbers rise. The Guardian.
